html:
The Jicarilla are an Eastern Apache people of northern New Mexico and southern Colorado. They speak a Southern Athabaskan language, and their name comes from Mexican Spanish for "little basket", after the small sealed baskets they used to carry water.

Their ancestors came south from Canada and reached the region by around 1500. They lived in the mountains and on the plains east of the Rio Grande, hunting bison and deer, and unlike most Apache they also farmed in river valleys. They traded with the Pueblo towns, especially Taos and Picuris. In the 1700s Comanche attacks pushed them off the plains into the mountains. After the United States took New Mexico in 1848 they fought the army in the 1850s, and in 1887 they were given a reservation at Dulce, New Mexico, where the Jicarilla Apache Nation still lives. The map also has a Jicarilla territory.
